model.label: Norman screen (GSE133344, K562 cells), PerturBench split: one regression per response gene, 881 response genes (879 use at least one sequence feature). Weight of a sequence = its feature's summed |coefficient| over all response genes x |f| of that sequence; a gene's weight = the sum over the sequences placed on it.
model.check: Model behind the card: delta_evaluation.tsv in the first folder reports macro Pearson delta 0.8884 on 45 held-out groups and 881 genes (median 0.9127; mean baseline 0.6511). The card value 0.890 is the PerturBench cosine (BENCH.seen.Norman on the Perturbation Response Prediction page, 43 doubles, 729 genes); that cosine is not stored in this folder. Coefficients: 279,380 rows, 23,523 sequence features with a non-zero coefficient, 879 response genes. Sequences: every feature's targets from f_table.tsv.gz (hash variant B), placed with the study's postprocess file (second path); f_table.tsv.gz here is byte-identical (md5 5a91515d) to the one in the 2026-09-14 Norman runs, whose log names this postprocess file (163,335,465 bytes), so both runs read the same sequences. All 23,523 features found in that file; all 475,416 full-length rows were split into start and target the way the model reads them, with the joined sequence checked unchanged; 6 short rows flagged and skipped. Exon or intron: GENCODE v46. Known variants and splice junctions (2026-10-29): own differences of each full sequence by BLAST to GRCh38 and GENCODE v46 transcripts (check_variants SEQUENCES.tsv); the run's star_junction column is empty, so junctions were computed here by spliced alignment. Card score 0.890: BENCH.seen.Norman on the Perturbation Response Prediction page (part 1). No run file holding 0.8904 was found in OUT_masked or in the GSE133344 launcher results. Known variant column: 2 sequences show "not checked" because other sequences with different bases share the same genome position, so the checked row could not be told apart.

note: Top sequence features of this model (by summed |coefficient| over all response genes). Feature 1: weight 35.2 over 99 response genes (mostly APOE, MS4A3, S100A11); its sequences fall on SEC61G, outside genes, CLC, H2AZ2, COX7A2L. Feature 2: weight 16.5 over 248 response genes (mostly HMGB2, MT-ND6, NEAT1); its sequences fall outside genes and on MT-CO3, MALAT1 / TALAM1, RPS29, GTF2I. Feature 3: weight 16.2 over 339 response genes (mostly NEAT1, MT-ND6, CALM2); its sequences fall outside genes and on RPS29, DHFR, MALAT1 / TALAM1, RAB3C. Feature 4: weight 13.6 over 33 response genes (mostly AIF1, LST1, SH3BGRL); its sequences fall outside genes and on SNRPEP4 / TINCR, DCAF6, PDHB, DANCR. Feature 5: weight 13.2 over 4 response genes (mostly COL1A1, SLC7A11, HRK); its sequences fall on ANAPC1, SKI, outside genes, MTCO3P12 / LINC00115, RPF2. 16% of the total weight is on sequences outside any gene or not placed. The genes with the most weight are mostly common to all cells (MALAT1, histones, ribosomal and mitochondrial genes); PRG2, CLC, LST1, CEBPE and the hemoglobin genes are the cell-type genes in the top 15, matching the granulocyte and red-cell programs reported for this screen. Rank = place among 11,021 named genes by summed weight; sequences of a gene include every sequence placed on it.
vc_note: Known variants: sequences whose own bases differ from the genome at a known dbSNP, ClinVar or COSMIC site (variant lookups: dbSNP via Ensembl release 116, ClinVar 2026-10-25, COSMIC v104). Sequences that fit another locus as well or better are not counted. Splice junction: the sequence matches a spliced transcript better than any single piece of the genome; ties are not counted.
